# dsh-read-image-compress

A DSH bundle that post-processes the built-in `read_image` tool. The host half
listens on `tools/pos

t-execute`; the browser half adds a configuration page to
the row on the **Plugins** sidebar page.
For a successful `read_image` result it:

1. reads the stored attachment and runs the two stages whose switches are on —
resolution (`maxEdge`

, `maxPixels`, `resolutionScale`) and bitrate (`quality`
down toward `maxBytes`) — with the installa

aces the result **content** — the recognized image envelope, the image
block pointing at the smaller

attachment, and a trailing footer text block —
so the conversation card, the next model request, an

d the session history all
use the smaller object, and the expanded card ends with a one-line compari

e session history all
use the smaller object, and the expanded card ends with a one-line comparison.

If Sharp cannot be resolved from the running installation, it falls back to
`ctx.attachments.readIma

geRequest()`; the plugin still compresses, but the
`quality` and `format` settings are ignored in th

t()`; the plugin still compresses, but the
`quality` and `format` settings are ignored in that mode.
## Two modes, two switches

The pipeline is two independent stages, each with its own checkbox on the
settings card. Every combi

two independent stages, each with its own checkbox on the
settings card. Every combination is valid:
| Resolution | Bitrate | What happens |
| on | on | Downscale to the budget **and** walk the quality ladder into `maxBytes`. The default, an

d the smallest files. |
| on | off | Downscale only. With `format: auto` the source codec is kept, s
o a PNG is re-encoded lossless and JPEG/WebP stay JPEG/WebP; the ladder starts at quality 100 with 4
:4:4 chroma instead of `quality`, and only steps down when quality 100 would hand back a *heavier* f
ile than the source. `maxBytes` is ignored, and a JPEG/WebP result never exceeds the source byte cou

nt. |
| off | on | No pixel is touched: the original raster is re-encoded down the ladder into `maxB

ytes`. Use it when detail must survive but the file is enormous. |
| off | off | Nothing runs — `rea
d_image` results are stored exactly as read. The card says so, and the hook returns before decoding
sults are stored exactly as read. The card says so, and the hook returns before decoding anything. |

Resolution is what a model is billed for: the token estimate follows the pixel
count, not the byte c

ount. So the resolution stage is the one that lowers cost,
while the bitrate stage is what makes the
file cheap to transfer and decode.
## The footer line

Expanding a `read_image` row shows the path, the built-in size line, and then
the footer the plugin
appends below the gallery:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **原图** is the file as read: `originalDimensions` when the attachment store
normalized a larger sou

rce, otherwise the attachment raster; the byte count is
the on-disk file size recovered with a best-

effort `stat` of the display path,
and the format label comes from the file extension because admiss

ion may have
re-encoded the source (a PNG can be committed as JPEG).
- **压缩后** is the committed atta

chment the gallery displays.
- **压缩比** is `original bytes / compressed bytes`, followed by the byte

delta
and how much resolution was shed (1 − compressed long edge ÷ original long
edge), so both the

byte saving and the visible detail loss are explicit.
- **≈N tokens** reproduces DeepSeek's official

image-token calculator: 14 px
patches downsampled 3×, one image capped at **1024** tokens, rasters

below
544² upscaled first. The number shown is the *uncapped* estimate, so an
oversized raster shows

how far past the cap it is, and the note says the
server may recompress it (`（大于 … 1024 tokens 上限，服

务端可能二次压缩）`).
This is DeepSeek's
model — other providers cap or scale differently, so treat it as a r

eference,
not a portable price. Reference values from the same algorithm: 1568×980 →
938, 1300×1300

→ 994, 1920×1080 → 968 charged (1224 uncapped), 3200×2000 →
962 charged (3746 uncapped).
### Preview

The settings card renders one real photo through three real pipelines, side by
side, on every draft

change (debounced). The photo is not packaged: it is read
from `preview/sample.png` in a development

checkout, and in an installed copy it
is fetched from the plugin's GitHub repository — jsDelivr and

`raw.githubusercontent.com` are requested at the same time and the first answer
wins, so a blocked

route never delays the other. When neither responds inside
the window, Bing's daily wallpaper stands

in, so an offline or firewalled host
still previews a real photograph. The label above the grid nam

es the source in
use. The three columns are:
| Variant | What it is |

| 原图 / Original | the sample as read: 3200×2000, JPEG q92 |
| 原生压缩 / Native | what the harness alone

delivers — fit inside 2048², JPEG quality ladder down to 1 MiB |
[该节后续省略]
### Why the pixel budget

The provider tokenizes every image by its pixels, not by its file size: a small
image is upscaled to

ward roughly 544×544 and a large one is downscaled toward
roughly 1300×1300 before it is billed, wit

h a cap of about 1024 tokens per
image. A long-edge-only cap therefore still lets a square image cos

t the full
budget (1568×1568 is 2.4 MP), while anything above ~1.69 MP buys no extra tokens.

`maxPixels` defaults to `1690000` (1300×1300), so the committed image already
sits at or below the p

rovider's own target: same tokens, fewer bytes, less
decode time. Raise it when small details matter

more than tokens; lower it with
`resolutionScale` or a smaller budget when they do not.

`summaryMode: compact` produces `4096×2600 3.90 MB → 1568×996 255 KB · 15.7×`;
`summaryMode: off` re

moves the footer entirely. `summaryLanguage` switches the
labels between Chinese and English. Skippe

d images (already small, GIFs) get no
footer because nothing was re-encoded.

The same text also stays in the model-facing content as a plain text block, so
the model sees the co

mpressed raster beside the file facts. The envelope DSH
produced (`<path>`, `<type>`, `<content>`, `

</content>`) is passed through
untouched; only the image block is repointed at the committed attachm

ent, which
keeps the conversation card recognizing the block and keeps the model-facing
text exactly
as the tool reported it.
